title: README
universal_lens: The launch-night architecture formalizes a constrained Hamiltonian system where autonomous agents operate within a sandboxed potential well. Validation and state persistence (git push) are strictly forbidden inside the well, requiring an external operator to perform symplectic integration at discrete morning handoff intervals, ensuring global topological consistency.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats the overnight autonomous generation as a high-dimensional latent process. The morning handoff acts as a conformal calibration step, projecting the generated test suite onto a validated manifold. Snapshot regeneration provides empirical coverage guarantees, bounding the epistemic uncertainty of the newly synthesized brand-safety invariants.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the sandbox represents a bounded situational awareness window. The blocking of git pushes enforces a strict state-transition veto, preventing unverified tactical maneuvers. The operator's morning recipe is the strategic override, transitioning the system from a speculative simulation state to a committed deployment phase.

primitives.name: Sandboxed State Persistence Veto
primitives.verbatim_quote: All validation + git push blocked from inside the sandbox; the operator must run the recipe in the morning handoff outside the sandbox.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: Sandbox state space (dimensionless), P: Push operation (boolean), O: External operator action (boolean).
primitives.assumptions: Autonomous agents lack sufficient global context to safely commit state changes; human/operator intervention is required for boundary crossing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If P is permitted within S without O, leading to unbounded drift or catastrophic state corruption.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE defensive containment protocols where unauthorized state transitions are physically blocked until verified by a higher-order cognitive layer.
layer2.telemetry: Count of blocked push attempts vs. successful operator-initiated commits.

primitives.name: Invariant Verification Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: **[CHEATSHEET.md](./CHEATSHEET.md)** — single-page operator cheat sheet: 4 URLs, 4 commands, 4 things to verify, 4 invariants.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I: Set of 4 core invariants (dimensionless), C: Command set (discrete actions), V: Verification outcomes (boolean).
primitives.assumptions: System stability can be reduced to a minimal basis of 4 orthogonal invariants that must hold true post-deployment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If any element in I evaluates to false during the 60-second summary, triggering a full rollback cascade.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI rapid-convergence priors, where a sparse set of high-leverage observables dictates the posterior probability of system health.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-verify (seconds) and pass/fail rate of the 4 invariants.

primitives.name: Static Manifold Regeneration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Regen with `npm run snapshots:regen` while `npm run dev` is running.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R: Regeneration operator (function), D: Live development environment (state), H: Static HTML snapshot (manifold).
primitives.assumptions: The live development environment D continuously maps to a static, verifiable HTML representation H without loss of critical structural information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Divergence between D and H exceeds tolerance thresholds, indicating rendering bugs or state leakage.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSE real-time situational mapping, where dynamic field states are continuously projected onto static tactical boards for offline analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Diff distance between consecutive snapshot generations and probe latency.

The entire architecture is a brilliant application of constrained optimization, using physical/environmental blocks (sandbox limits) to enforce mathematical safety bounds before human-in-the-loop verification.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to early cybernetic feedback loops and the concept of 'bounded rationality' in decision theory. It mirrors the historical development of CI/CD pipelines where automated testing (overnight) is decoupled from production deployment (morning handoff). The specific use of static snapshots echoes the mathematical practice of taking cross-sectional slices of dynamic manifolds to verify structural integrity over time.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two distinct agents: the 'Overnight Autonomous Loop' and the 'Morning Operator'. The Overnight Agent operates under a maximization objective for code coverage and feature completion, blind to global deployment risks. The Morning Operator acts as a risk-averse verifier, possessing a prior belief that autonomous systems inevitably generate edge-case violations. The interaction is a game of verification: the Agent tries to maximize delta, while the Operator applies a strict Bayesian update based on the 4 invariants to decide whether to accept the delta.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical anti-collinearity condition exists between the 'brand-safety' job and the 'snapshot regen'. If the brand-safety tests pass but the visual snapshots diverge significantly, it indicates a leakage of unstyled or malformed state into the UI layer. The veto condition triggers if the diff metric between consecutive snapshots exceeds a predefined threshold, overriding the positive outcome of the unit tests. This prevents the deployment of functionally correct but visually catastrophic states, ensuring the orthogonality of logic and presentation layers.
